label: D2 after a common a2 -> S2 transition
explanation: Fires only at DELAY_2, and only when the agent chose a2 and reached S2 (the common a2 transition). Both are observed inputs at D2: in_action=2 and in_state=2. Dev precision is 0.85, recall about 1.0 (1 missed step), F1 0.92. It never fires at D1 or GO, on S1, or on rare transitions. Requiring S2 alone (also counting rare a1->S2) drops precision to 0.66, so the feature needs the conjunction of action and state. Magnitude follows the model value output: the top value bin has a 47% firing rate and 52% of the activation mass, and adding value > 7.7 lifts precision to 0.98 but cuts recall to 0.71. The false positives are a2/S2c steps with low value; it also rarely fires near the episode end (trials 90-99), where value drops. Reward and good state matter only through value. No future variables are used.

issues: The core claims hold. On dev, all activation is at D2 (D1 and GO have 0 active steps). It fires only when in_action=2 and in_state=2 (one active step out of 183,887 at in_state=1) and essentially never on rare transitions (1 active step at common=0). Test scores for the base predicate reproduce: P 0.846, R 1.0, F1 0.916. With S2 alone, test P is 0.652. Misses are only 3 tiny steps.

Systematic false-positive class: the end of the episode. On test, (base) & (ep_trial>=90) has precision 0.19, and (base) & (ep_trial>=95) has precision 0.011, so the feature is almost silent in the last 5 trials. This class is about 13k of the 24.5k false positives, more than half. Trials 80-89 still have precision 0.72-0.86, so the drop is sharp.

The explanation says the end-of-episode drop is a value effect. It is not: (base) & (ep_trial>=90) & (value>5) still has only precision 0.57 on test, against 0.92 for value>5 before trial 90. So 'reward and the good state affect it only through value' is not supported. Episode position has its own effect beyond what value captures.

Smaller systematic class: switch trials after an unrewarded a1 trial (prev_action==1 & prev_reward==0), where (base) & (ep_trial<90) has precision 0.20 on test. Switch trials in general (prev_action==1) have precision 0.48.

Restricting to ep_trial<90 raises test F1 from 0.916 to 0.955 (P 0.930, R 0.981). Also excluding the a1-unrewarded switch case gives test F1 0.958. Value>5 alone gives test F1 0.950 but leaves the end-of-episode class only partly explained.
